hints: The speed keeps rising as long as the acceleration is positive. When does it stop rising? The gain is the area under the a–t graph up to then.
worded:
1. a = 5 − (5/6)t, positive until 6 s. So the speed grows all the way to 6 s: that is the maximum.

2. Velocity gained = area of the a–t triangle: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 m/s.

3. For (ii), integrate twice: v = 5t − (5/12)t², and x = (5/2)t² − (5/36)t³. At 2 s: 10 − 10/9 = 80/9 ≈ 8.9 m.

4. Sense check: at a constant 5 m/s² it would cover 10 m in 2 s; the acceleration is falling, so a little less.
mistakes: Maximum speed is where a = 0 (at 6 s), not where a is largest (at 0 s).
Don’t use s = ½at² with a = 5: the acceleration is falling.
